thread:
maya: quick flag — onboarding llama2-mini-v1 into hosted shows a prompt truncation by one token when using our chat template. repro below, can someone triage? :eyes:

maya: repro prompt: 
```
User: Tell me a short story about a frog.
Assistant:
```
maya: tokenizer output (hosted): `[101, 350, 405, ..., 2]` (counts 1 less than local. eos id appears shifted)

ashok: interesting. did we point to the same tokenizer.json as the weights? path?

maya: weights: gs://redwood-models/llama2-mini/v1/weights.safetensors
maya: tokenizer: gs://redwood-models/llama2-mini/v1/tokenizer.json (confirmed present)

priya: can you paste the model config we load on hosted? maybe add_bos/add_eos flags mismatch.

maya: hosted config snippet: 
```
{"model_name":"llama2-mini","bos_token_id":null,"eos_token_id":2,"add_bos_token":false,"chat_template":"standard_v2"}
```

jen: hmm boto behavior: when bos_token_id is null our runtime will insert a synthetic BOS (id 0) for streaming paths unless add_bos_token is explicitly false in both tokenizer and model config. that could cause off-by-one in prefix cache.

chad: @maya can you try this quick local check? run tokenization with HF tokenizer file and compare with hosted runtime: 
```
>>> tok.encode("User: Tell me a short story about a frog.\nAssistant:")
```
chad: also include `repr(tok.all_special_ids)`

maya: ran it locally — output length 45 and ids end with 2. local all_special_ids = [0, 2]
maya: hosted runtime gave length 44, all_special_ids = [2]

eva: sounds like hosted dropped BOS. could be layering issue: chat template preprends prompt with BOS at compile time for some models. if model config and tokenizer disagree, caching/batching can trim first token on streamed responses.

priya: low-effort mitigation: set `add_bos_token=true` in hosted model config and bump model GC to pick up. but we should root cause — where is the loader setting for synthetic BOS?

ci-bot: deploy note: model-config update requires a minor rollout (canary -> 10%) and takes ~7m to propagate to hosted pools. see infra runbook link: https://console/ops/runbooks/model-config-updates

maya: created quick PR #4127 (config change + unit test) — pinging for review. includes a small tokenization assert and a comparison test against local tokenizer.

jen: I'll take a look. if we decide to set add_bos true, add a comment explaining why and add a one-line migration note for Dedicated/private so customers know the change.

ashok: long-term fix: runtime should consult tokenizer.special_tokens_map and avoid inserting synthetic BOS if tokenizer already declares it. filing an infra ticket for that: INF-887.

chad: for immediate triage @jen can you review PR and if ok, approve so we can canary? maya will run a targeted test after canary.

maya: thanks! I'll queue a repro run post-canary and post results here. will also verify embedding routes (token index offsets matter for QA).

jen: on it, aim to review in next 30m. if we hit flakiness, rollback plan: revert config and open a hotfix branch. :ok_hand:

maya: update: canary started (2160001289). running token diff now. will update soon.

maya: update (2160001388): canary looks good — token counts match local now. patching rollout to 50%.

chad: sweet. pls file a short postmortem note in eng-ml channel later with the root cause and action items.

maya: will do. tl;dr: mismatch between hosted model config and tokenizer special token declarations caused host to omit synthetic BOS — fixed by aligning `add_bos_token` and adding runtime check ticket.
